questions: Are rows and columns 1-indexed as implied by the description (i=1..N) and coordinates (i,i) to (j,j), or should the implementation use 0-indexed internal representation while still outputting rows in order?
When overwriting colors, does 'overwrite' mean completely replace the color of those cells with the new color, regardless of previous color?
What characters represent black and white? Should '#' be black and '.' be white as shown in the example pattern?
Is N guaranteed to be odd, even, or either? The pattern description doesn't specify parity constraints.
For the rectangle from (i,i) to (j,j), are both endpoints inclusive? The description says 'top-left cell is (i,i) and bottom-right cell is (j,j)' but doesn't explicitly state inclusivity.
Should the output be printed exactly as described, with no extra spaces or newlines beyond the N lines each of length N?
If N=1, i=1 and j=1, so i ≤ j, and i is odd. Should the single cell be filled black? The operation seems applicable but the pattern example starts at N=11.
Is the initial 'no cell is colored' equivalent to all white, or some other uncolored state that gets overwritten? Since overwriting happens, initial color doesn't matter.
